newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Zenith Q4 faces uphill struggle.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Zenith Q4 faces uphill struggle.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp will be plagued in the fourth quarter by the same problems that led it to report a third-quarter loss of $0.61 per share, said Peter Willmott, newly elected president and chief operating officer.
"I'm not making any predictions, but the problems we encountered in the third quarter will have some spinoff (effect) in the fourth quarter," Willmott said in a telephone interview.
Glenview, Ill.-based Zenith said gross margins were down in the third quarter due to lower selling prices and delays in new model shipments for higher-margin consumer electronics products.
Willmott said turning around the struggling consumer electronics and network systems company may mean adding to some product categories and cutting others. He declined to specify.
"For the short term, we may make additions to our product line and maybe prune some product categories," he said, declining to specify which product lines would be altered.
"It's going to take a review of every system we have," he said.
Willmott has been a Zenith director since 1990 and its interim head since late July.
A fourth-quarter writeoff is likely, analysts said.

Citing the competitive television market and delays by the company in getting new chassis for its 30 inch and larger sets, analyst Robert Gutenstein of Kalb Voohris & Co said he expects Zenith to report another loss in the fourth quarter.
Gutenstein also lays heavy odds on some fourth-quarter writeoff by the company as it trims unprofitable operations.

Zenith currently has an estimated 15 percent share of the U.S. television market, and Willmott said he would like to see that increase. "Getting that division to be more effective and capable of picking up market share is a top priority," he said.
Willmott said recent new contracts fueled optimism that Zenith is on track for a turnaround.
In September, Zenith won a contract worth a potential $1 billion to make three million digital terminals for the Americast telecommunications consortium.

"That puts us in the forefront of the digital category (as the industry shifts from analog), but its financial payoff is a couple of years away," said Willmott, noting that first shipments of the new devices will not occur until mid-1997.
"Zenith has...the capability to become a world-class company," Willmott added.
Prior to joining Zenith, Willmott was president and chief operating officer of Federal Express Corp and formerly CEO of retailer Carson Pirie Scott & Co.
Analysts describe him as a no-nonsense, direct person who knows how to ask the right questions.
